newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul allows seven firms to do business with North.
newsitem.headline: Seoul allows seven firms to do business with North.

text.p: South Korea on Friday gave approval to seven domestic companies to contact North Koreans for business for the first time since a submarine incursion in September plunged ties to a new low.

The seven companies include trading firm LG International Corp, garment maker Shin Won Corp, drug maker Korea Green Cross Corp, and sewn goods maker Taechang Co Ltd, a statement from Seoul's Unification Ministry said.
The firms are seeking business in North Korea in such sectors as drug making, beverage production, mineral water production and textiles production, the statement said.

All contacts with the North were frozen after a Shark-class North Korean submarine dropped 26 armed intruders on a Southern beach in September. Pyongyang issued a rare apology last month and Seoul immediately returned the remains of 24 infiltrators who were shot and killed. One was captured alive and the other is still at large.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not in a peace agreement.
